activity_context.topic_title: Differentiating an Inverse Function at a Point

feedback.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3x$ and the point $P(\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{3\pi }{2})$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$ calculate ${({f}^{-1})}^{′}(\frac{3\pi }{2}).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{3\pi }{2}).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3x \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =3-\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{3\pi }{2})$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(\frac{3\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(\frac{3\pi }{2}) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(\frac{3\pi }{2}))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
